attribution: Wood dose rates assume chips or cubes in a homebrew-scale vessel and are far higher per litre than a barrel's surface-to-volume ratio would give. Extraction rate depends on format, toast, temperature and alcohol — the ranges here are starting points for a tasting schedule, not endpoints.

additives.name: Grape Tannin (red)
additives.description: Condensed tannin from grape skins and seeds, used to build structure and stabilise colour.
additives.usageNotes: Added at crush it binds with anthocyanin to fix colour; added later it adds grip and mouthfeel.
additives.cautions: Easy to overshoot into bitterness. Bench-trial at 0.1 g/L increments.
additives.attribution: scottlabs.com does not resolve and never did — the supplier's domain is scottlab.com, singular. Repointed to the product category section; Scott Laboratories publishes its figures in the annual Fermentation Handbook, which is the document behind these numbers.

additives.name: Grape Tannin (white)
additives.description: A gentler tannin preparation for whites and rosés, protecting against oxidation without adding perceptible astringency.
additives.usageNotes: Also used pre-fermentation to inhibit the laccase enzyme carried by botrytised fruit.
additives.cautions: Overdosing shows as a hard, drying finish rather than obvious bitterness.
additives.attribution: scottlabs.com does not resolve and never did — the supplier's domain is scottlab.com, singular. Repointed to the product category section; Scott Laboratories publishes its figures in the annual Fermentation Handbook, which is the document behind these numbers.

additives.name: Quebracho Tannin
additives.description: A robust, inexpensive condensed tannin from South American quebracho wood.
additives.usageNotes: Common in cider for adding the grip that dessert-apple juice lacks.
additives.cautions: Coarser than grape tannin — noticeable as woody astringency if overdone.
additives.attribution: scottlabs.com does not resolve and never did — the supplier's domain is scottlab.com, singular. Repointed to the product category section; Scott Laboratories publishes its figures in the annual Fermentation Handbook, which is the document behind these numbers.

additives.name: Oak Tannin (hydrolysable)
additives.description: Ellagitannins extracted from oak, the compounds that give barrel-aged drinks their structure independent of any oak flavour.
additives.usageNotes: Adds the tannic contribution of a barrel without the vanillin and lactone flavours.
additives.cautions: Consumes oxygen readily, which is part of the point, but means it can mask a genuine oxidation problem.
additives.attribution: scottlabs.com does not resolve and never did — the supplier's domain is scottlab.com, singular. Repointed to the product category section; Scott Laboratories publishes its figures in the annual Fermentation Handbook, which is the document behind these numbers.

additives.name: Black Tea
additives.description: The traditional country-wine tannin source: a cup of strong tea per gallon.
additives.usageNotes: Works, and costs nothing. Brings its own tea flavour, which suits some meads and country wines.
additives.cautions: Far less predictable than a measured oenological tannin.

additives.name: French Oak
additives.description: Tight-grained European oak, air-dried for two to three years. Subtler and more tannic than American oak, with spice and cedar rather than sweet vanilla.
additives.usageNotes: Chips extract in days, cubes in weeks, staves and spirals in months, a barrel in years. Typical chip dose is 2-4 g/L.
additives.cautions: Chips give a flatter, faster extraction than cubes — more oak, less integration. Taste weekly and pull early.

additives.name: American Oak
additives.description: Higher in lactones than European oak, giving the coconut, vanilla and dill signature of bourbon and Rioja.
additives.usageNotes: By US law a straight whiskey must use a new charred oak container, which is why used bourbon barrels are cheap and plentiful for everyone else.
additives.cautions: The coconut lactone note is polarising and hard to remove once extracted.

additives.name: Hungarian Oak
additives.description: Botanically the same species as much French oak, grown more slowly; often described as sitting between French and American in character.
additives.usageNotes: Historically much cheaper than French oak, which is most of its appeal.
additives.cautions: Quality varies more by cooper and seasoning than by origin.

additives.name: Oak Toast Levels
additives.description: Toasting thermally degrades the wood's lignin and hemicellulose, and the degree of toast changes the flavour more than the oak's origin does.
additives.usageNotes: Light toast keeps raw wood tannin and fresh sawn character. Medium develops vanillin, caramel and coconut. Heavy pushes into smoke, clove and coffee, and destroys much of the vanillin. Charring, a separate and more extreme process, creates a carbon layer that also strips sulphur compounds — the basis of bourbon maturation.
additives.cautions: Reference entry, not a dosable product.

additives.name: Cherry Wood
additives.description: Softer and fruitier than oak, with almond and stone-fruit notes and much less tannin.
additives.usageNotes: Popular for sour beers and fruit spirits where oak tannin would dominate.
additives.cautions: Less structurally sound than oak for actual barrels; usually used as chips or spirals.

additives.name: Maple Wood
additives.description: Mild and sweet with little tannin — contributes texture and a faint sweetness rather than structure.
additives.usageNotes: Sometimes used for finishing whiskies and for barrel-aged beers.
additives.cautions: Very low tannin, so it will not firm up a soft drink.

additives.name: Chestnut Wood
additives.description: Very high in hydrolysable tannin — historically used across southern Europe where oak was scarce.
additives.usageNotes: Traditional for some Italian and Spanish wines and for Armagnac.
additives.cautions: Porous and tannic; extracts far faster and harder than oak.

additives.name: Mizunara Oak
additives.description: Japanese oak, prized for a sandalwood, coconut and incense character that develops only over long maturation.
additives.usageNotes: The signature of Japanese whisky finishing.
additives.cautions: Notoriously porous and leaky as a barrel wood, and expensive. The character takes many years to emerge.
